chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

Qatad ibn Du'ama came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and he said: 'O Qatad, are you the Faqih (jurist) of the people of Basra?' He said, 'That is what they allege.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'It has reached me that you interpret the Quran.' Qatad said to him, 'Yes.' He said to him: 'Do you interpret it by knowledge or by ignorance?' He said, 'No, by knowledge.' He said to him: 'So if you interpret it by knowledge, then you are you and I will ask you.' Qatad said, 'Ask.'
He said: 'Inform me about the Statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in Saba: "And We apportioned for them the journey therein; travel through them by night and by day in security."'
Qatad said, 'That is for the one who goes out from his house with lawful provisions, a lawful mount, and lawful rental, intending this House (the Kaaba); he is safe until he returns to his family.'

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'I adjure you by Allah, O Qatad, do you know that a man may go out from his house with lawful provisions, a lawful mount, and lawful rental, intending this House, but the road is cut off for him, his expenses are lost, and he is struck with a blow that causes his exhaustion?' Qatad said, 'Yes, by Allah.'

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Woe to you, O Qatad, if you have interpreted the Quran from your own self, then you are destroyed and you have destroyed (others); and if you have taken it from the men (others), then you are destroyed and they are destroyed.'

'Woe to you, O Qatad, that is for the one who goes out from his house with provisions and a lawful mount, aspiring for this House, knowing our rights, whose heart yearns for us, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "So make the hearts of some people yearn towards them."'

'And it does not mean the House, for He says 'towards them'. So we are, by Allah, the supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Whoever has a heart that yearns for us, his Hajj is accepted; otherwise, no. O Qatad, if it is like that, he is safe from the punishment of Hell on the Day of Resurrection.'
Qatad said, 'Certainly, by Allah, I will not interpret it except like this.'
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Woe to you, O Qatad, only those who are addressed by the Quran truly know it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the true meaning of 'security' in the verse about traveling to the Kaaba according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this dialogue, Imam al-Baqir critiques Qatadah ibn Di'ama’s literalist interpretation of Surah Saba 18, arguing that mere physical safety during pilgrimage is insufficient without spiritual recognition of the Ahl al-Bayt. The Imam emphasizes that true 'security' (amān) is contingent upon the heart's yearning for the Imams, linking the verse to Ibrahim’s supplication in Surah Ibrahim 37, and concludes that the Quran is only truly understood by those directly addressed by it.
